userOutcome: Users can create households, invite members by email, assign roles, and switch between personal and household contexts. Solo users have zero overhead.
scopeSummary: Household bounded context (internal/household/): Household aggregate root (Members as child entities, Role value object, invariants: exactly one owner, max 10 members), Invitation separate aggregate (token lifecycle). Command handlers, HouseholdContext middleware, permission matrix, token-based email invitation, audit log, domain events. Next.js household switcher.
risks: Permission model complexity — 4 roles x 15+ actions
Every downstream query must use HouseholdContext middleware
Household aggregate invariants must be enforced at domain level
readinessReason: Research provides complete schema, permission matrix, middleware patterns, UX flows, and DDD aggregate design with invariants.
handoffSummary: Implement internal/household/ bounded context: Household aggregate with Members + Role value object, Invitation aggregate. Command handlers. HouseholdContext middleware. Permission enforcement. Audit log. Domain events (MemberAccepted triggers cross-context category seeding). Next.js household switcher + member management.
